slides.title: Two questions at the counter
slides.text: When you collect a parcel, Pim checks two different things. Authentication proves it is really you. Authorization checks the list to see if this parcel is yours to open.

slides.title: Know, have, are
slides.text: Sign-in checks come in three kinds. Two different kinds protect you far better than two of the same kind.
steps: code sent to a phone: something you have
slides.alt: The Pro mailbox key builder: a passphrase made of chosen words, different from every other account key.

slides.title: Passkeys, honestly
slides.text: A passkey lives on your device, which proves it is you without sharing a copyable secret. A fake page cannot trick you into handing it over, because there is nothing to hand over.

slides.title: Shared screens, separate doors
slides.text: On a shared tablet or class account, profiles and permissions matter. Your profile keeps your work, messages and settings separate from everyone else who uses the same screen.

words.means: proving it is really you, not someone pretending to be you
checking that you are allowed to see or do something
signing in with two different kinds of check, not just one
a key kept on your device that proves it is you

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Packet Post at Lock It and play the levels you have not played yet. Notice each check: is it proving who you are, or checking what you may open?
slides.alt: Lock It in Pro opens with the sharing sort: security starts with knowing what must be protected.
